subject: Theft in the temple of democracy
alt: Cartoon: two men run off with sacks on their backs, one marked MPs, MLAs and the other SIR. A rat sitting by a hole in the wall says: even in the temple of democracy, a big theft is going on.
chutki: In the old days when there was a theft in a temple, the rats got the blame, for the prasad laddoos they nibbled. This time Dhodapkar has made the rat a witness. He sits at the mouth of his hole, watching in amazement what is being carried off by the sackful.

One sack holds MPs and MLAs, the other SIR. That is, the representatives are being carried off and so are those who choose the representatives. The thieves' faces are not seen, only their backs and sacks, because in a democracy big thefts often happen with the back turned. Look at the rat's standing: in this temple he is now the most honest one left.
